refusal_reason: Officially retracted source; content declared unreliable by the publisher, so no sovereign primitive can be extracted in good faith. The PDF is technically readable (14 pages, full text layer, all read), but page 1 is the Hindawi/Wiley retraction notice (Computational and Mathematical Methods in Medicine, Volume 2023, Article ID 9864250, published 1 November 2023, DOI 10.1155/2023/9864250) retracting Song & Hu, 'Data Fusion Algorithm for Myocardial Proteomics and Its Research in Sports' (Volume 2022, Article ID 4049169, DOI 10.1155/2022/4049169). The notice cites evidence of systematic manipulation of the publication process: discrepancies in scope, discrepancies in the research description, discrepancies between data availability and the research described, inappropriate citations, incoherent/meaningless/irrelevant content, and peer-review manipulation, and states explicitly that the article's content is unreliable. Independent full-text inspection confirms the indicators: (1) p.3 falsely attributes the proteome concept to 'two German scientists, Williams and Wilkin' in 1941 (the term was coined by Marc Wilkins in 1994); (2) p.3 duplicates an entire mass-spectrometry paragraph verbatim; (3) the printed 'information entropy' Eq. (3), S(i) = -sum f_i*chi_f, has no logarithm and no probability normalization and is not a valid entropy; Eqs. (10)-(11) mix node coordinates, a tensor product, and a cubed distance into an 'energy consumption' expression that is dimensionally incoherent; (4) p.11 compares the operation group against itself ('1.3% and 14.7% higher than those in the operation group and the model group'); (5) Figure 7 (p.12) plots 'applications of cardiac proteomics in sports science' across school subjects 'Math, English, Physics'; (6) citations are inappropriate, e.g. ref [11] (Turkish high-school sport attitudes) supports a MALDI-TOF-MS rat-cardiac-proteomics claim and ref [12] (Indian pharmaceutical industry competitiveness) supports an mRNA biology claim; (7) abstract and conclusion swap group attributions for the 13.7%/16.2% contraction-velocity figures. Extracting verbatim 'invariants' from this source would launder manipulated content into the Foundry primitives table and downstream RLVR synthesis. Per doctrine, honest refusal beats fabrication: the source is epistemically inaccessible as a sovereign reference even though its bytes are readable. No primitives, traces, or mappings are asserted from this article.
